title: Acute Pyelonephritis in Pregnancy: Assessment, Admission and Follow-Up

evidenceAudit.scope: Pregnant patients with suspected acute pyelonephritis; recognition, cultures, hospital assessment and obstetric follow-up.
findings: The named primary guideline was opened and the cited sections were used.
Normal values are descriptive; use local laboratory and age/pregnancy ranges.
unverifiedSections: No topic-specific Saudi national guideline was identified in the opened Saudi MOH protocol index.
SFDA registration and hospital formulary availability were not verified; no drug dose is supplied.

pathophysiology.summary: Ascending urinary infection can involve the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Pregnancy-related urinary stasis increases the risk of upper-tract infection. Systemic infection can cause sepsis, acute kidney injury and uterine activity.
keyMechanisms: Ascending urinary infection can involve the renal pelvis and parenchyma.
Pregnancy-related urinary stasis increases the risk of upper-tract infection.
Systemic infection can cause sepsis, acute kidney injury and uterine activity.

symptoms: Fever or rigors with flank or back pain.
Dysuria, frequency, urgency, nausea or vomiting may coexist.
physicalSigns: Fever, tachycardia, hypotension, dehydration or uterine activity.
redFlags: Sepsis physiology, hypotension, altered mental state, oliguria, persistent vomiting or concern about preterm labour.
precipitants: Recent urinary infection, urinary obstruction, renal stone, diabetes or urinary instrumentation.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Urinary symptoms without fever or flank tenderness.
Colicky pain and haematuria; fever raises concern for infected obstruction.
Focal abdominal signs without a urinary source; pregnancy can alter pain location.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Fever with flank pain or costovertebral-angle tenderness plus urinalysis/culture evidence supports acute pyelonephritis.
Refer if signs suggest sepsis or serious illness, dehydration or inability to take oral fluids/medicines; pregnancy lowers the threshold for specialist assessment (NG111 1.1.4–1.1.5).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Pyuria and/or nitrite; haematuria may occur
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Supports a urinary source but does not replace culture.
Obtain before antimicrobials when this does not delay treatment; tailor therapy to the result.

ruleIn.testName: Full blood count, renal profile and lactate when systemically unwell
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Inflammatory response, acute kidney injury or raised lactate
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Stages systemic illness and informs fluid and antimicrobial safety.

ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Use when obstruction, stone, abscess or failure to improve is suspected.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess mother and fetus
actions: Use an ABCDE assessment, record sepsis physiology and obtain obstetric review.
Send urine culture before treatment when feasible; do not delay emergency treatment in sepsis.

clinicalManagement.title: Admit or obtain urgent specialist assessment
actions: Pregnancy with suspected upper urinary infection requires obstetric/medical assessment and a low threshold for admission.
Escalate suspected infected obstruction to urology.

clinicalManagement.title: Review response and results
actions: Review culture and narrow treatment through the local antimicrobial pathway.
Reassess persistent fever, pain or physiological abnormality for obstruction, abscess or an alternative diagnosis.

medicationPlan.note: NICE lists antimicrobial options, but pregnancy-specific local resistance, product availability and dose adjustment require the hospital antimicrobial pathway. No medicine dose may be prescribed from this draft. Use the current Saudi hospital formulary and specialty-approved protocol; verify allergy, pregnancy/age, renal and hepatic function.

teaching.scope: Pregnant patients with suspected acute pyelonephritis; recognition, cultures, hospital assessment and obstetric follow-up.
learningObjectives: Recognise the condition and its red flags.
Choose initial tests without delaying urgent escalation.
Use a named multidisciplinary disposition plan.
keyPoints: Sepsis physiology, hypotension, altered mental state, oliguria, persistent vomiting or concern about preterm labour.
Review culture and narrow treatment through the local antimicrobial pathway.
pitfalls: Delaying escalation while waiting for non-essential tests.
Using an unverified medicine regimen instead of the current local protocol.

patientEducation: Explain the working diagnosis, immediate plan and specific return or deterioration signs.
lifestyleAndDiet: Address prevention and self-management only after the acute safety plan is complete.
dischargeCriteria: Afebrile and haemodynamically stable, tolerating oral intake, fetal/obstetric concerns addressed, culture follow-up and return plan documented.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Confirm culture response and arrange obstetric follow-up; repeat urine testing only as directed by the obstetric or microbiology plan.
